headline: KYURI DESIGNS WHERE
DIGITAL MEETS
EVERYDAY LIFE
paragraphs: With a background in Industrial, Graphic, and UX Design, I create brand and digital experiences.
I play with AI to make something new, anywhere.

qa.q: What did you want to be as a kid?
qa.a: An architect. I grew up poring over buildings in magazines, and at Temple University I took architecture classes and interned in spatial UX at Philly Fashion Week. I never became one. Instead, I ended up working on the rebrand of Clayco, an architecture and construction company.

A fresh start, and the buildings. I came for an M.S. in HCI at DePaul and fell in love with the city. My favorites: the tulips in front of the Wrigley Building every May, and Jeanne Gang's Aqua tower.

qa.q: Industrial, graphic, UX: isn't that a lot?
qa.a: In Korea I studied industrial and graphic design: 3D products, mobility, and home goods, then apps, posters, and books. Grad school added research and storytelling. Different scales, same subject: how people actually live.

qa.q: How do you actually use AI?
qa.a: To rework the design process itself. At Clayco, we used AI and new tools to make the early stages of a rebrand faster and cleverer. I've kept testing that in my own projects, like [TypeLab](/work/typelab/) and [Clack](/work/clack/).

qa.q: What's the oldest project you're still working on?
a: [Light Life](/work/light-life/), a lamp for the winter blues.
2023: My team won a business competition with it at Temple University.
2024: I redesigned the lamp and its website for my graduation show at Sejong University.
2026: I rebuilt its app: tell it your day and your city, and it suggests the light you need.
From an object to a screen, it has grown the way I have.

qa.q: What are you looking for next?
qa.a: Work where digital meets real lives and real spaces, using everything I've picked up along the way: industrial design, graphic design, and a love of architecture. As for where: anywhere. I love exploring.
